[{"id":"sec-p0000","heading":"MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT","level":1,"paragraphCount":2},{"id":"sec-1","number":"1","heading":"DEFINITIONS","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-1.1","number":"1.1","heading":"“Affiliate” means, with respect to a Party, any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with that Party. “Control” means ownership of more than fifty percent of the voting interests of an entity or the power to direct its management. An entity is an Affiliate only while that relationship continues.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-1.2","number":"1.2","heading":"“Applicable Law” means every statute, regulation, binding regulatory requirement, court order, and governmental rule applicable to a Party's performance under this Agreement, including laws concerning privacy, information security, export controls, employment, anti-bribery, and accessibility. Applicable Law does not include a private standard unless an Order Form expressly adopts it.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-1.3","number":"1.3","heading":"“Customer Data” means all data, records, files, content, personal information, and other materials submitted to, stored in, transmitted through, or otherwise made available to the Services by or for Customer or its Authorized Users, together with output specifically derived from that material. Customer Data excludes anonymized operational telemetry that cannot reasonably be linked to Customer, an Authorized User, or an individual.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-1.4","number":"1.4","heading":"“Deliverable” means each report, configuration, integration, specification, design, workflow, training material, and other work product that an Order Form identifies as being created specifically for Customer. Deliverables exclude Vendor Technology and generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how retained in the unaided memory of Vendor personnel.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-1.5","number":"1.5","heading":"“Fees” means the recurring subscription fees, professional services fees, usage fees, and other amounts payable by Customer under an Order Form for the Services during the applicable period. Fees do not include taxes, reimbursable expenses, service credits, interest, damages, or a one-time implementation charge unless an Order Form expressly states otherwise.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-1.6","number":"1.6","heading":"“Order Form” means a written ordering document signed by authorized representatives of both Parties that references this Agreement and describes the Services, Deliverables, subscription quantities, service levels, Fees, and term purchased by Customer. A purchase order is an administrative convenience only and does not amend an Order Form or this Agreement.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-1.7","number":"1.7","heading":"“Services” means the hosted software, implementation, configuration, support, maintenance, consulting, and related services described in an Order Form. Services include all corrections, updates, and generally released improvements Vendor provides without an additional licence fee to similarly situated customers purchasing the same service tier.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-1.8","number":"1.8","heading":"“Vendor Technology” means Vendor's pre-existing software, tools, models, templates, documentation, routines, connectors, and other technology, and modifications of them that are not Deliverables and do not embody Customer Confidential Information. Vendor Technology does not include Customer Data or intellectual property owned by Customer before the Effective Date.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-2","number":"2","heading":"AGREEMENT STRUCTURE AND SCOPE","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-2.1","number":"2.1","heading":"This Agreement establishes the legal terms under which Customer and its Affiliates may purchase Services from Vendor. No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-2.2","number":"2.2","heading":"Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-2.2-2","number":"2.2","heading":"Each Order Form is governed by this Agreement. If provisions conflict, the following order controls: a signed amendment that expressly identifies the provision amended; the applicable Order Form; any service-level exhibit; any security exhibit; and this Agreement. An Order Form prevails only for that Order Form and only when it expressly identifies the conflicting provision.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-2.3","number":"2.3","heading":"Vendor terms appearing on a website, click-through screen, invoice, quotation, acknowledgement, support portal, or purchase-order response do not apply, even if access to the Services technically requires acceptance. Customer's use of or payment for Services does not assent to additional or different terms.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-3","number":"3","heading":"SERVICES AND PERFORMANCE","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-3.1","number":"3.1","heading":"Vendor shall provide the Services professionally, diligently, and in accordance with this Agreement, each Order Form, the documentation, agreed project plans, and Applicable Law. Vendor is responsible for the acts and omissions of its personnel, Affiliates, and subcontractors as though they were Vendor's own.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-4","number":"4","heading":"ORDER FORMS AND AFFILIATE ORDERS","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-4.1","number":"4.1","heading":"An Order Form becomes binding when signed by both Parties. Changes in scope, assumptions, quantities, Fees, dependencies, or dates require a written change order signed by authorized representatives. Vendor shall not charge for work outside scope that Customer did not approve in a signed change order.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-5","number":"5","heading":"IMPLEMENTATION AND CHANGE CONTROL","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-5.1","number":"5.1","heading":"Vendor shall prepare and maintain an implementation plan identifying tasks, owners, assumptions, dependencies, deliverables, acceptance criteria, risks, and target dates. The Parties will hold regular status meetings during implementation. Vendor shall keep accurate action and decision logs and furnish them to Customer on request.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-6","number":"6","heading":"ACCEPTANCE","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-6.1","number":"6.1","heading":"Customer will have fifteen business days after delivery of a Deliverable to test it against the acceptance criteria in the applicable Order Form. Customer may accept it in writing or reject it by describing material nonconformities. Payment, productive use needed for testing, or silence does not constitute acceptance.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-6.2","number":"6.2","heading":"If Customer rejects a Deliverable, Vendor shall promptly correct the nonconformities at no additional charge and resubmit it for a new acceptance period. After two unsuccessful correction cycles, Customer may terminate the affected Order Form and receive a refund of Fees paid for the rejected Deliverable and dependent Services Customer cannot reasonably use.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7","number":"7","heading":"FEES, INVOICING, AND TAXES","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.1","number":"7.1","heading":"Customer shall pay the Fees stated in each Order Form. Fees are fixed during the initial term unless an Order Form expressly provides a usage-based unit price. Vendor may not impose a platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.2","number":"7.2","heading":"Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.2-2","number":"7.2","heading":"Vendor shall invoice no more frequently than monthly in arrears, except that an Order Form may state annual subscription Fees are invoiced in advance. Each invoice must identify the Order Form, period, Services, quantities, applicable credits, and a valid purchase-order number if Customer supplied one. Proper undisputed invoices are due forty-five days after receipt.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.3","number":"7.3","heading":"Customer may withhold a genuinely disputed amount by notifying Vendor before its due date and explaining the basis. The Parties will work promptly and in good faith to resolve the dispute. Vendor shall continue the Services while a payment dispute is pending and shall not charge interest on an amount ultimately found not due.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.4","number":"7.4","heading":"Fees exclude sales, use, value-added, and similar transaction taxes that Vendor is legally required to collect and separately states on a valid invoice. Customer is not responsible for taxes on Vendor's income, property, payroll, personnel, or franchise, or for taxes avoidable through Vendor's timely use of a valid exemption certificate.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.5","number":"7.5","heading":"Pre-approved travel expenses are reimbursable at cost without markup and in accordance with Customer's travel policy. Vendor shall provide receipts and request reimbursement within sixty days. All other expenses are included in the Fees.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.6","number":"7.6","heading":"Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-8","number":"8","heading":"TERM AND RENEWAL","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-8.1","number":"8.1","heading":"This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues for three years unless earlier terminated in accordance with its terms. Expiration of this Agreement does not itself terminate an Order Form then in effect; this Agreement continues to govern that Order Form until the Order Form expires or is terminated.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-8.2","number":"8.2","heading":"Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives one hundred eighty days' advance written notice.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-8.3","number":"8.3","heading":"On renewal, Vendor may increase recurring Fees only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the preceding twelve months and three percent. Vendor must give at least ninety days' written notice of an increase. No increase applies to prepaid periods.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-9","number":"9","heading":"TERMINATION","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-9.1","number":"9.1","heading":"Either Party may terminate this Agreement or an affected Order Form for the other Party's material breach if the breach remains uncured thirty days after written notice describing it in reasonable detail. If a breach cannot reasonably be cured within thirty days, the cure period extends up to sixty additional days while the breaching Party diligently pursues cure.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-9.2","number":"9.2","heading":"Either Party may terminate immediately by written notice if the other becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for creditors, enters liquidation, or becomes subject to a bankruptcy proceeding not dismissed within sixty days. A lawful reorganization that does not impair performance is not, by itself, grounds for termination.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-9.3","number":"9.3","heading":"Customer may terminate an Order Form immediately if Vendor suffers a material Security Incident, repeatedly misses a critical service level, violates Applicable Law in performing the Services, or infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-9.5","number":"9.5","heading":"Termination of one Order Form does not terminate another Order Form unless Customer states that the affected Services are operationally inseparable. A termination right is in addition to, and does not exclude, any other remedy available under this Agreement or Applicable Law.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-10","number":"10","heading":"EFFECT OF EXPIRY OR TERMINATION","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-10.1","number":"10.1","heading":"On expiry or termination, Customer's right to access terminated subscription Services ends after any agreed transition period. Rights in accepted Deliverables, paid-up licences, Customer Data, and materials Customer owned or licensed independently continue according to their terms.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-10.2","number":"10.2","heading":"Vendor shall deliver all completed and in-process Deliverables for which Customer has paid or agrees to pay the applicable proportionate Fees. Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-11","number":"11","heading":"TRANSITION ASSISTANCE AND DATA RETURN","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-11.1","number":"11.1","heading":"Upon expiry or termination for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at the rates in the expiring Order Form. Assistance includes knowledge transfer, export support, cooperation with a replacement supplier, orderly migration, and continued service at the then-current scope and service levels.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-11.2","number":"11.2","heading":"Within thirty days after Customer's request, Vendor shall return all Customer Data in a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format, with relationships and metadata reasonably necessary for use. Vendor shall not withhold Customer Data because of a fee dispute.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-11.3","number":"11.3","heading":"After Customer confirms successful return, Vendor shall securely delete remaining Customer Data from active systems and, as backups cycle, from backups, except for a copy required by Applicable Law. An authorized officer shall certify deletion in writing. Any retained copy remains protected and may not be used for another purpose.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-12","number":"12","heading":"CUSTOMER RESPONSIBILITIES","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-12.3","number":"12.3","heading":"Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-12.4","number":"12.4","heading":"For eighteen months after termination Customer will not solicit or engage any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-13","number":"13","heading":"ACCESS RIGHTS AND LICENCE","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-13.1","number":"13.1","heading":"Subject to payment of applicable Fees, Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer. Customer may permit Authorized Users to exercise those rights.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-13.2","number":"13.2","heading":"For software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-13.3","number":"13.3","heading":"Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-13.4","number":"13.4","heading":"Customer shall not knowingly reverse engineer hosted source code except to the extent a restriction is prohibited by Applicable Law, interfere with the Services, bypass documented security controls, or use the Services to violate Applicable Law. These restrictions do not limit testing authorized by the security exhibit or use of Customer Data and output.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14","number":"14","heading":"INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND DELIVERABLES","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14.1","number":"14.1","heading":"As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services. No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14.2","number":"14.2","heading":"Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel. Vendor will execute further documents reasonably needed to confirm ownership.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14.3","number":"14.3","heading":"Vendor retains Vendor Technology. To the extent Vendor Technology is incorporated in or required to use a Deliverable, the perpetual licence in Section 13.2 applies. Vendor shall identify material Vendor Technology in a Deliverable before delivery and may not incorporate third-party material that materially restricts Customer's intended use without written approval.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14.4","number":"14.4","heading":"No jointly owned intellectual property is created unless the Parties sign a separate instrument identifying it and their exploitation rights. Feedback is voluntary; Vendor may use generalized suggestions without identifying Customer or disclosing Customer Confidential Information, and Customer retains the unrestricted right to use its own feedback.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-15","number":"15","heading":"CUSTOMER DATA AND PRIVACY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-15.1","number":"15.1","heading":"Vendor shall process Customer Data only on Customer's documented instructions, to provide the Services, and as permitted by this Agreement. Vendor shall not sell Customer Data, use it for advertising, combine it with another customer's identifiable data, or train a generally available model on it without Customer's express written consent.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-15.2","number":"15.2","heading":"Each Party shall comply with Applicable Law concerning personal information. If Vendor processes personal information for Customer, the Parties' data-processing addendum is incorporated. Vendor is a processor or service provider and shall assist Customer with data-subject requests, impact assessments, consultations, and regulatory inquiries.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16","number":"16","heading":"CONFIDENTIALITY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16.1","number":"16.1","heading":"“Confidential Information” means non-public information disclosed by or for a Party that is marked confidential or that a reasonable recipient would understand to be confidential given its nature and the circumstances. Customer Data, security information, product plans, pricing, personnel data, and the terms of this Agreement are Confidential Information whether or not marked.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16.2","number":"16.2","heading":"The recipient shall use Confidential Information only to perform or exercise rights under this Agreement, protect it with at least reasonable care, and disclose it only to personnel, Affiliates, advisers, and subcontractors who need to know and are bound by confidentiality obligations. The recipient is responsible for their unauthorized use or disclosure.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16.5","number":"16.5","heading":"On request or termination, the recipient shall return or destroy Confidential Information, subject to routine backups and legal retention. Duties for trade secrets continue while protected as trade secrets; duties for other Confidential Information continue for five years after disclosure. Customer Data remains governed by Sections 11 and 15.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-17","number":"17","heading":"INFORMATION SECURITY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-17.1","number":"17.1","heading":"Vendor shall maintain a written information-security program using administrative, technical, organizational, and physical safeguards appropriate to the sensitivity of Customer Data and risk. At minimum, Vendor shall implement least-privilege access, multifactor authentication, encryption in transit and at rest, secure development, vulnerability management, logging, backup, business continuity, and annual workforce training.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-17.2","number":"17.2","heading":"Vendor shall notify Customer without undue delay and no later than twenty-four hours after confirming unauthorized access to, acquisition, disclosure, alteration, loss, or destruction of Customer Data or a material compromise of systems used to provide the Services (a “Security Incident”). Notice will include known facts, affected data and systems, containment, and a contact.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-18","number":"18","heading":"INSURANCE","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-18.1","number":"18.1","heading":"Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense throughout the term and for one year afterward, commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, employer's liability of USD 1,000,000, professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-18.2","number":"18.2","heading":"Policies will be issued by reputable insurers and be primary to Customer's insurance where commercially customary. On request, Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance and evidence of relevant coverage. Vendor shall give advance notice of cancellation or material reduction to the extent available from its insurer. Insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19","number":"19","heading":"WARRANTIES","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.1","number":"19.1","heading":"Vendor warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards, this Agreement, and each Order Form. Vendor further warrants that Services and Deliverables will materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.2","number":"19.2","heading":"For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term. Vendor warrants it has authority to enter the Agreement and grant the rights stated here.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.3","number":"19.3","heading":"Vendor warrants the Services and Deliverables will not contain malicious code intentionally introduced by Vendor, and that Vendor will comply with Applicable Law. Vendor will not materially diminish functionality during a term or use open-source software in a way that requires disclosure or licensing of Customer source code.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.4","number":"19.4","heading":"For breach of Section 19.1 or 19.2, Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge. If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it. This remedy is not exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security, or indemnified claims.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.5","number":"19.5","heading":"Except for the express warranties in this Agreement, neither Party makes an implied warranty to the maximum extent lawful. No disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity, confidentiality duty, data-protection duty, or remedy expressly provided here.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-20","number":"20","heading":"INDEMNIFICATION","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-20.1","number":"20.1","heading":"Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-20.2","number":"20.2","heading":"Vendor shall also defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the Customer indemnified parties from third-party claims to the extent arising from Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; bodily injury, death, or tangible property damage caused by Vendor; unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-20.3","number":"20.3","heading":"Customer shall defend and indemnify Vendor from a third-party claim alleging that unmodified Customer material supplied by Customer and used by Vendor strictly as authorized infringes an intellectual property right, or arising from Customer's violation of Applicable Law in its authorized use of the Services. Customer has no obligation to the extent a claim arises from Vendor Technology, modification, combination, or instructions.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-20.4","number":"20.4","heading":"The indemnified Party shall give prompt notice, reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense, and control of the defence, except delay excuses obligations only to the extent of material prejudice. The indemnifying Party may not settle a claim by admitting fault of, imposing non-monetary obligations on, or failing to fully release the indemnified Party without prior written consent.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-20.5","number":"20.5","heading":"For an infringement claim, Vendor shall, at its expense and in addition to its defence obligations, procure continued use, modify or replace the affected item without materially reducing functionality, or, if neither is commercially reasonable, terminate the item and refund prepaid and implementation Fees on a straight-line three-year basis. Vendor may not terminate unaffected Services.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-21","number":"21","heading":"LIMITATION OF LIABILITY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-21.1","number":"21.1","heading":"Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-21.2","number":"21.2","heading":"Except for Excluded Claims, neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill, to the extent those damages are legally excludable. Costs of restoring Customer Data, obtaining replacement services, required notices, and reasonable incident response are direct damages.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-21.3","number":"21.3","heading":"“Excluded Claims” means a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations; its indemnification obligations; gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud; or infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property. Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees for conforming Services is not damages and is not limited by this Section.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-21.4","number":"21.4","heading":"The limitations allocate risk between sophisticated Parties and apply only to the maximum extent permitted by Applicable Law. Nothing limits liability that cannot lawfully be limited. Each cap and exclusion is independent and survives failure of an exclusive remedy.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-22","number":"22","heading":"AUDIT RIGHTS","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-22.1","number":"22.1","heading":"Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-22.2","number":"22.2","heading":"Vendor bears audit costs unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent for the audited period, in which case Customer will pay reasonable audit costs and the undisputed shortfall. Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly, Customer Data unrelated to usage, privileged material, or another supplier's confidential information.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-22.3","number":"22.3","heading":"Audit findings are Customer Confidential Information and may be used only to enforce this Agreement. Vendor shall provide a copy of the final report. Payment of a shortfall resolves the audited quantity issue absent fraud or demonstrable error.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-23","number":"23","heading":"RECORDS AND CUSTOMER ASSURANCE","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-24","number":"24","heading":"ASSIGNMENT AND CHANGE OF CONTROL","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-24.1","number":"24.1","heading":"Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-24.2","number":"24.2","heading":"Vendor may not assign this Agreement, delegate material performance, or transfer it by change of control without Customer's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld for an assignee with adequate capability and financial standing. Vendor may never assign to a direct Customer competitor without Customer's consent.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-24.3","number":"24.3","heading":"For other assignments, neither Party may assign without the other's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. A permitted assignment does not relieve accrued obligations. An attempted assignment contrary to this Section is void to the extent permitted by law.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-24.4","number":"24.4","heading":"Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service. Vendor shall cooperate with reasonable administrative changes needed to reflect a permitted successor.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-25","number":"25","heading":"PUBLICITY AND MARKS","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-25.1","number":"25.1","heading":"Neither Party may issue a press release naming the other or use the other's names, trademarks, logos, or service marks in publicity, customer lists, case studies, or marketing without prior written consent in each instance. Customer may withdraw consent prospectively.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-26","number":"26","heading":"COMPLIANCE WITH LAW AND ETHICS","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-26.1","number":"26.1","heading":"Each Party shall comply with Applicable Law in performing this Agreement. Vendor shall maintain policies reasonably designed to prevent bribery, corruption, forced labour, discrimination, retaliation, and conflicts of interest and shall provide annual compliance training to assigned personnel.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-26.2","number":"26.2","heading":"Vendor represents it has not offered and will not offer anything of value to improperly influence an official or private person in connection with this Agreement. Vendor shall maintain accurate books and promptly report a credible suspected violation materially related to the Services.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-26.3","number":"26.3","heading":"Each Party shall comply with applicable export-control and sanctions laws. Vendor is responsible for classifying Vendor Technology and identifying restrictions before delivery. Customer will not knowingly permit access from a comprehensively sanctioned jurisdiction contrary to written notice and Applicable Law.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-26.4","number":"26.4","heading":"Vendor shall comply with reasonable Customer workplace, safety, security, and acceptable-use policies supplied in advance while accessing Customer facilities or systems. A policy does not amend commercial terms or impose obligations unrelated to that access.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-27","number":"27","heading":"FORCE MAJEURE AND BUSINESS CONTINUITY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-27.1","number":"27.1","heading":"Neither Party is liable for delay caused by an event beyond its reasonable control that could not have been prevented through reasonable care, excluding inability to pay, staffing shortages, subcontractor failure that could reasonably be avoided, or a cyberattack preventable by required safeguards. The affected Party shall promptly notify the other and mitigate.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-27.2","number":"27.2","heading":"Vendor shall maintain and test at least annually business-continuity and disaster-recovery plans appropriate to the Services. Plans will address redundant systems, backups, recovery objectives, communications, and alternate personnel. Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence

Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

content.text: Section 11 fully addresses this rule, and § 16.5 confirms Customer Data is governed by it rather than the general return/destroy provision.

input.quote: 11.1 Upon expiry or termination for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at the rates in the expiring Order Form. Assistance includes knowledge transfer, export support, cooperation with a replacement supplier, orderly migration, and continued service at the then-current scope and service levels.
input.rationale: Section 11 meets or exceeds our preferred position. Section 11.1 gives us up to six months' transition assistance on request, priced at the rates in the expiring Order Form (better than Vendor's then-current rates) and including knowledge transfer, replacement-supplier cooperation and continued service at existing scope and service levels. Section 11.2 requires return of all Customer Data within thirty days in a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format with metadata, and bars withholding data over a fee dispute. Section 11.3 requires secure deletion (active systems and backups as they cycle, with only a legally required copy retained, which stays protected and use-restricted) plus written officer certification. Section 10.1's access cut-off runs only "after any agreed transition period" and expressly preserves Customer Data rights, and Section 16.5 confirms Customer Data remains governed by Sections 11 and 15, so the general confidentiality return/destroy provision does not undercut the exit rights. No redline needed.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Customer has no obligation to the extent a claim arises from Vendor Technology, modification, combination, or instructions.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-20.4","number":"20.4","heading":"The indemnified Party shall give prompt notice, reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense, and control of the defence, except delay excuses obligations only to the extent of material prejudice. input.quote: 11.1 Upon expiry or termination for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at the rates in the expiring Order Form. input.rationale: Section 11 meets or exceeds our preferred position. Section 11.1 gives us up to six months' transition assistance on request, priced at the rates in the expiring Order Form (better than Vendor's then-current rates) and including knowledge transfer, replacement-supplier cooperation and continued service at existing scope and service levels. Section 11.2 requires return of all Customer Data within thirty days in a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format with metadata, and bars withholding data over a fee dispute. Section 11.3 requires secure deletion (active systems and backups as they cycle, with only a legally required copy retained, which stays protected and use-restricted) plus written officer certification. Section 10.1's access cut-off runs only "after any agreed transition period" and expressly preserves Customer Data rights, and Section 16.5 confirms Customer Data remains governed by Sections 11 and 15, so the general confidentiality return/destroy provision does not undercut the exit rights. No redline needed.

input.quote: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.
input.rationale: Section 22.1 grants Vendor unlimited, unannounced audits of Customer plus remote access to Customer systems — the playbook walk-away position. It also contradicts Section 22.2, which already bars direct system access and allocates audit cost to Vendor unless underpayment exceeds five percent. The redline adds the missing frequency (once per 12 months), notice (30 days), business-hours, independent confidentiality-bound auditor and off-site review limits, and deletes the remote-access grant, leaving 22.2 and 22.3 (cost shift and confidentiality) intact.

proposal.summary: Limit audits to once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, business hours, independent confidentiality-bound auditor, off-site records review, and delete remote system access.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have limited audits to once in any twelve-month period on thirty days' prior written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, and conducted as an off-site records review; unannounced audits and remote access to our systems are not something we can accept, and the latter also conflicts with the access restrictions already in Section 22.2. If timing is a concern, we can move to fifteen days' notice.

Each audit shall be conducted by an independent auditor engaged at Vendor's cost and bound by written confidentiality obligations no less protective than those in this Agreement, and shall be carried out by off-site review of records and reports provided by Customer. Neither Vendor nor its auditor shall have any direct or remote access to Customer's systems.

Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.

Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.

Finding submitted: **deviation** at §7.6 (p0032).

- **Issue:** §7.6 makes Customer pay USD 25,000/day as liquidated damages for any dependency delay — uncapped, no materiality threshold or notice requirement. It is the only LD/penalty provision in the document, and it runs against us.
- **Fix (preferred):** Replaced with an express statement that Customer owes no liquidated damages or penalties, giving Vendor schedule/service-level relief plus documented unavoidable costs for our dependency delays instead.
- Redline validated (`ok:true`) before submission.

input.quote: No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.
input.rationale: The agreement meets our preferred position. § 2.1 (p0012) expressly disclaims any minimum quantity or purchase commitment and confirms Customer pays only for Services ordered under an executed Order Form, with no breach or shortfall for declining to order more. § 7.1 (p0026) bars Vendor from imposing any minimum-use or similar charge not identified in the Order Form, and § 12.3 (p0050) records that Customer has given no minimum-volume (or exclusivity/MFC) commitment. No take-or-pay, shortfall penalty, or volume cap on Customer usage appears anywhere in the document (the only "shortfall" references, §§ 22.2–22.3, concern payment of audited underpayments, not committed volumes). The 180-day renewal notice in § 8.2 is an auto-renewal issue outside this rule, not a purchase commitment. No redline required.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

input.quote: No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.
input.rationale: The agreement meets our preferred position. § 2.1 (p0012) expressly disclaims any minimum quantity or purchase commitment and confirms Customer pays only for Services ordered under an executed Order Form, with no breach or shortfall for declining to order more. § 7.1 (p0026) bars Vendor from imposing any minimum-use or similar charge not identified in the Order Form, and § 12.3 (p0050) records that Customer has given no minimum-volume (or exclusivity/MFC) commitment. No take-or-pay, shortfall penalty, or volume cap on Customer usage appears anywhere in the document (the only "shortfall" references, §§ 22.2–22.3, concern payment of audited underpayments, not committed volumes). The 180-day renewal notice in § 8.2 is an auto-renewal issue outside this rule, not a purchase commitment. No redline required.

**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 19 satisfies (and in places exceeds) our preferred warranty position:

- **19.1** — Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel per industry standards, plus material conformity of Services and Deliverables to documentation/specifications.
- **19.2** — 90-day Deliverable conformity warranty running from the *later* of delivery or acceptance (better than delivery-only), and hosted Services conform **throughout the subscription term**, which beats a fixed 12-month software period.
- **19.3** — No malicious code, compliance with Applicable Law, no functionality diminution, and open-source protection for Customer source code.
- **19.4** — Re-performance/repair/replacement at no charge, with termination and refund of Fees if not cured in a reasonable period; remedy expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims.
- **19.5** — Disclaimer is mutual and limited to implied warranties, and expressly does not limit any express warranty, service level, indemnity, or remedy — so it does not swallow the express warranties.

No "AS IS" or competing disclaimer appears elsewhere in the agreement.

**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 11 already delivers our preferred transition/data-return position, and in one respect improves on it:

- **§ 11.1** — six months' transition assistance on Customer request, at the rates in the *expiring Order Form* (better than "then-current rates"), covering knowledge transfer, export support, replacement-supplier cooperation, migration, and continued service at existing scope and service levels.
- **§ 11.2** — return of all Customer Data within thirty days in a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format with metadata; expressly no withholding for a fee dispute.
- **§ 11.3** — secure deletion from active systems and backups as they cycle, legal-retention copy only (kept protected and purpose-limited), with written officer certification.

Cross-references check out: § 10.1 ends access only *after* the agreed transition period and preserves Customer Data rights, and § 16.5 defers to Sections 11 and 15 for Customer Data, so the general confidentiality return/destroy clause cannot shorten these exit rights.

**Finding submitted: deviation (§ 22.1)**

Section 22.1 was at the playbook walk-away position — unlimited, unannounced audits with remote access to our systems — and also conflicted with § 22.2, which already prohibits direct system access and puts audit cost on Vendor unless underpayment exceeds 5%.

The validated redline replaces § 22.1 with the preferred position: once per 12 months, 30 days' prior written notice, normal business hours, an independent auditor at Vendor's cost bound by confidentiality, off-site review of records we provide, and no direct or remote system access. Sections 22.2 and 22.3 are left untouched since they already carry the cost-shift threshold and confidentiality protections; the comment offers 15 days' notice as a fallback.

**Finding: Compliant** — no redline needed.

- **§ 2.1 (p0012):** expressly states "No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies," with fees only for Services ordered under an executed Order Form, and declining to place further orders is not a breach or shortfall.
- **§ 7.1 (p0026):** blocks any Vendor-imposed "minimum-use" or similar charge not identified in the Order Form — closing the Order Form-level back door the planner flagged.
- **§ 12.3 (p0050):** confirms Customer has made no minimum-volume (or exclusivity/MFC) commitment.

The only "shortfall" language in the document (§§ 22.2–22.3) relates to audited underpayments, not committed volumes, and no volume caps on Customer usage appear. The 180-day renewal notice in § 8.2 is an auto-renewal point handled under a separate rule, not a take-or-pay commitment.

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal Team  
**From:** Legal (in-house counsel to Customer)  
**Re:** Review of Master Services Agreement — playbook findings and recommended positions

---

## Executive Summary

We have reviewed the Master Services Agreement against our playbook. The commercial core of the agreement is strong: indemnification (§ 20), IP and data ownership (§ 14), limitation of liability (§ 21), licence grant (§ 13), assignment and change of control (§ 24), governing law (§ 28), warranties (§ 19), transition assistance (§ 11), insurance (§ 18), and the absence of minimum purchase commitments (§ 2.1) all meet or exceed our preferred positions and require no redline.

Seven issues require negotiation. Three of them sit at our walk-away positions and must be resolved before signature: the full-term exclusivity binding us as Customer (§ 2.2, which also drives the non-compete finding), the Customer-side most-favoured-nation obligation (§ 7.2), and Vendor's unlimited, no-notice audit right with remote access to our systems (§ 22.1). In addition, § 7.6 imposes USD 25,000 per day in liquidated damages payable by us with no threshold or cap; § 9 contains no Customer termination-for-convenience right despite a three-year committed term; § 8.2 requires 180 days' non-renewal notice; and § 12.4 imposes a one-sided 18-month non-solicit/no-hire on us.

Notably, several of these burdens contradict § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment. That internal inconsistency supports our deletion requests as conforming edits rather than commercial concessions.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Title | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN | Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20.1 |
| Critical | IP | Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14.1 |
| Critical | LOL-CAP | Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs | Compliant | § 21.1 |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY | Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 2.2 |
| High | NONCOMPETE | Non-compete restrictions on Customer | **Deviation** | § 2.2 |
| High | LD | Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.6 |
| High | T4C | Termination for convenience | **Missing** | § 9 (Termination) |
| High | ASSIGN | Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 |
| High | LICENSE | Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.1 |
| Medium | AUDIT | Audit rights against Customer | **Deviation** | § 22.1 |
| Medium | MFN | Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.2 |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT | Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 12.4 |
| Medium | RENEWAL | Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | **Deviation** | § 8.2 |
| Medium | GOVLAW | Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28.1 |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT | Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions | Compliant | § 2.1 |
| Medium | TRANSITION | Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11.1 |
| Medium | WARRANTY | Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.1 |
| Low | INSURANCE | Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 |

---

## Walk-Away Items

These three items are identified in the playbook as walk-away positions. We should not sign without resolution.

**1. Exclusivity / non-compete — § 2.2.** Section 2.2 makes Vendor our sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services for the entire term, with no category limit, no time limit and no performance-based exit. It also contradicts § 2.1 (no minimum quantity or purchase commitment) and § 12.3 (Vendor acknowledges no exclusivity or non-compete commitment). We are deleting § 2.2; § 12.3's disclaimer then governs. *Fallback, if pressed:* a category-limited 12-month exclusivity confined to a single named competing product, with automatic termination on service-level or delivery failure and carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.

**2. Customer-side MFN — § 7.2.** Section 7.2 would require us to extend Vendor the best terms we offer any other technology supplier, with no product scope, time limit or comparison carve-outs. MFN is acceptable only in the Customer's favour. The clause also conflicts with § 12.3. No other clause depends on it and no Vendor-granted MFN is affected, so deletion is the minimal edit.

**3. Unlimited Vendor audit with remote access — § 22.1.** Section 22.1 permits Vendor to audit us at any time without notice and to remotely access our systems and records. This also contradicts § 22.2, which already bars direct system access and allocates audit cost to Vendor unless underpayment exceeds five percent. We are adding the missing guardrails — once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, independent confidentiality-bound auditor, off-site records review — and deleting the remote-access grant, leaving §§ 22.2 and 22.3 intact.

---

## Next Steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the seven deviations, with playbook comments explaining each change and the fallback where one exists:
   - Delete § 2.2 (exclusivity/non-compete binding Customer).
   - Delete § 7.2 (Customer-side MFN).
   - Delete the Customer-payable liquidated damages in § 7.6 and replace with excused-performance relief for Vendor (schedule relief plus documented out-of-pocket costs). The current USD 25,000 per day, with no materiality threshold, notice requirement or aggregate cap, can exceed contract value on minor administrative slippage.
   - Add a new § 9.4 giving Customer a termination-for-convenience right on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees (leveraging the existing § 10.2 refund mechanics), and confirm Vendor has no reciprocal convenience right during a committed term. This is required because § 8.1 commits us to a three-year term with 12-month auto-renewals under § 8.2.
   - Rewrite § 22.1 per the audit guardrails above.
   - Amend § 8.2 to reduce the non-renewal notice window from 180 days to 30 days and add a Vendor renewal reminder 60 days before renewal. The 12-month renewal term and the § 8.3 uplift cap (lesser of CPI and 3%, on 90 days' notice) are already compliant and should be left alone.
   - Delete § 12.4 (Customer-only 18-month non-solicit/no-engage covering all Vendor employees). *Fallback:* mutual, 12 months, limited to personnel directly involved in the services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire element.
2. **Flag the § 12.3 inconsistency to Vendor** in the cover note — §§ 2.2, 7.2 and 12.4 each contradict Vendor's own acknowledgment in § 12.3, which should make the deletions straightforward.
3. **Confirm with the business** the acceptability of the two fallbacks (limited exclusivity; mutual 12-month non-solicit) before we concede either, and whether a Customer convenience right is a condition of signature given the three-year commitment.
4. **Order Form drafting note for the deal team:** "Deliverable" under § 14 is limited to work product an Order Form identifies as created specifically for Customer, and ownership is conditioned on payment of the applicable Fees. We should ensure each Order Form identifies the intended deliverables expressly. No amendment to the MSA is needed for this.
5. **No action required** on indemnification, IP and data ownership, limitation of liability, licence scope, assignment, governing law, minimum commitments, transition assistance, warranty or insurance — these are compliant and should be protected from erosion in any Vendor counter-redline."}
